The Lost Incarnate

Odibael Zebanund has heard that I am the outlander claiming to fulfill the Nerevarine Prophecies. He wished me no ill, but told me that I am yet another False Incarnate, and that pursuing the Prophecies further would lead only to my death.

After showing 'One-Clan-Under-Moon-And-Star' to Zebanund, he accepted that I must truly be the Nerevarine. He explained that he was once a traveling companion of the previous False Incarnate, Peakstar. He had been holding out hope for years that she might return. He wanted to know if in my travels, I had come across any trace of her.

I explained to Zebanund that I met the ghost of Peakstar in the Cavern of the Incarnate, and showed him a possession of Peakstar as proof of my claims. He was doubtful of my claims, but admitted he felt I was telling the truth. He asked me if I would visit Peakstar once more to ask her why she went off on her own. The man is clearly desparate for some closure.

Peakstar explained that the only way she felt she could prove herself as the Nerevarine was to take on the Sixth House directly. She failed and wishes for me to tell Odibael that she is sorry for everything. She also told me that he has one of her possessions, a staff, hidden away. "He intends to give it to you all ready. I can feel it even as I watch him now. Tell him these words, and he shall know the truth of your claims," she said.
Before I left the Cavern of the Incarnate, Peakstar had one more gift for me. She granted me a blessing, and said that she would do her best to watch over me.
I returned to Zebanund and told him all that Peakstar had said. He gifted me the staff of which Peakstar had spoken. He wished me good fortune as I follow the Path of the Nerevarine.
A Stolen Relic

Odibael Zebanund at Bal'laku has asked me to help retrieve a relic of the Urshilaku that was stolen long ago by a group of outcasts from his tribe. The relic is a glove that grants elmental powers to its wearer. Zebanund says that there were once five among the group of outcasts, though he is unsure if they all still travel together. One of these outcasts was called Mausur Assaplit.

I have found and returned the 'relic' glove to Zebanund. Aside from its enchantment which was decently powerful, it was quite unremarkable; hardly something that I would call a relic. Zebanund was very grateful to have it returned, but I can't help but feel that there is something more he isn't telling me. He bestowed upon me an Urshilaku blessing of Azura.
Odibael Zebanund, the Ashlander at Bal'laku, now refuses to speak to with me. It seems I will have no dealings with him in the future.
Odibael Zebanund, the Ashlander at Bal'laku, attacked me after I caused him great offense. It is now obvious that I will have no dealings with him in the future.
I have passed the test of wisdom of Odibael Zebanund, the Ashlander at Bal'laku. He offered me the hospitality of his home, and is now willing to answer my questions.

Outlander, this is indeed the glove I was looking for. I thank you for returning it to me. It is... good to have it back. I'm truly sorry outlander, but I haven't anything tangible to give you in return. Let me bestow upon you a traditional Urshilaku blessing of Azura (Odibael mutters a quick prayer). Know that the Lady of Twilight smiles upon you outlander.

I recently spotted an outcast from the Urshilaku tribe that I suspected might have perished long ago. I pursued him, but he fled into the foothills of Red Mountain and I have been unable to track him down. I care not for the fate of the outcast, only for the fate of an object that might be in his possession. Many years ago this outcast and the group he traveled with stole a relic of the Urshilaku. I want that relic returned. The outcast is Mausur Assaplit.

What you describe are obviously dreams from the Sharmat, but I have never heard of someone recieving ones as clear as the ones you've experienced. I wonder what it could mean, and I wonder what part you will have to play in all of this, outlander...

What you describe are obviously dreams from the Sharmat, but I have never heard of someone who isn't a Dunmer recieving ones as clear as the ones you've experienced. It is strange that they should occur for you.

I serve as a guardian for this sacred place against those who would do it harm. The outlanders and House Dunmer who occasionally travel through here are hardly a true problem. What I truly speak of are the Mabrigash - dark witches who use this site's magick for their own ill purposes. You had best be careful if you run across any, outlander.

Mausur Assaplit once traveled with a group of five outcasts from our tribe, though I do not know how many still travel with him. The relic they stole was a glove that grants its wearer the power of fire, frost, and shock. It was made by one of the most skilled enchantresses of the Urshilaku. If you can find this relic I would be very grateful if you would return it here to me. I do not know where Assaplit is hiding, though you might try searching the foothills southeast of here beyond the Dwarven ruins.

You are not first to take my test, but you are the first in many, many years. Every day out here is a struggle, outlander. I do not have the luxury of engaging in conversation with every traveler I meet, so I must make sure someone is worthy of my time.

Keep your wits about you out here. There's no telling what you'll run into out here. Outcasts and Mabrigash will attack most outlanders on sight, and that is to say nothing of the blighted creatures and corprus beasts found out here.
I have no secrets anymore. At least not with you friend.
I have my secrets like anyone else, outlander, and I would prefer that they remain secret.
Ashlanders know few rumors, and myself even fewer. I'm sorry.
Very well, Nerevarine. Go now with my blsessing.

I have found that my power from my past life has waned less than the others here, and I choose now to bestow that power upon you Nerevarine, in the form of a blessing. In what way would you choose for this blessing to manifest itself?
The Erabenimsun care only for making war. They have the strength of true ashlanders, but none of the wisdom.
[Odibael Zebanund refuses to speak to you or even aknowledge your presence.]

I am sorry that it is not to your liking, outlander, but you had better get used to it out here. By the way... I am called Odibael Zebanund. I am of the Urshilaku clan, though I have not had any interactions with them in quite some time. Now, I am willing to answer your questions. Would you like to know more of Bal'laku? Or would you like to know about my purpose here? Or perhaps... would you be willing to provide me with aid?

I am called Odibael Zebanund. I am of the Urshilaku clan, though I have not had any interactions with them in quite some time. Now, I am willing to answer your questions. Would you like to know more of Bal'laku? Or would you like to know about my purpose here? Or perhaps... would you be willing to provide me with aid?
First, let me provide you with the hospitality of my home, humble as it may be.

Again correct... I must admit that you have impressed me outlander. You clearly know much of Resdayn, but that was obvious to me when I first saw you. You found yourself this deep within the Ashlands, and are very much alive. That alone was proof of some of your knowledge and competence.

Yet another baseless lie of the Temple - known by few, and believed by even fewer of its own disciples. I am sad to learn that you apparently count yourself among them. You have failed my test. For some reason, I thought you might be different... That wisdom guided you. I can see now I was wrong. I will do you no harm outlander, but I must insist that you leave this place and do not return. We will have no further dealings between us.

A valiant guess, and you are close to the correct answer, but alas, no. Nerevar died on Red Mountain. This is undisputable. You have failed my test. For some reason, I thought you might be different... That wisdom guided you. I can see now I was wrong. I will do you no harm outlander, but I must insist that you leave this place and do not return. We will have no further dealings between us.
My final question - Why did I call this a holy place? What happened here long ago?
Correct. If Azura is the loving mother of Resdayn, then Boethiah and Mephala are its stern fathers, challenging the Dunmer and making us stronger for it.

You are a fool if you believe the Aedra have any concern for the Dunmer, or any people of this world for that matter. You have failed my test. For some reason, I thought you might be different... That wisdom guided you. I can see now I was wrong. I will do you no harm outlander, but I must insist that you leave this place and do not return. We will have no further dealings between us.

The Tribunal are wretched and false gods, who betrayed their oaths to Nerevar. They care nothing for this land or its people. They care only about maintaining their power, and prolonging their unnatural lives - the foul ghouls that they are. You have failed my test. For some reason, I thought you might be different... That wisdom guided you. I can see now I was wrong. I will do you no harm outlander, but I must insist that you leave this place and do not return. We will have no further dealings between us.
My next question - Who are the three true gods of Resdayn and the Dunmeri?
Correct. The meaning of the name Resdayn has been lost to the ages, but all true Dunmer, ashlander and settled alike, know it as the name of this land.

It is true that in the past, this land was called Veloth by some, and even now some of my people prefer this name, but this is not the name of which I speak. This is not Nerevar's name for this land. You have failed my test. For some reason, I thought you might be different... That wisdom guided you. I can see now I was wrong. I will do you no harm outlander, but I must insist that you leave this place and do not return. We will have no further dealings between us.

While some Dunmer now use this name, it is a wretched word of the Cyrodiils. It has nothing at all to do with this land or its people. You have failed my test. For some reason, I thought you might be different... That wisdom guided you. I can see now I was wrong. I will do you no harm outlander, but I must insist that you leave this place and do not return. We will have no further dealings between us.
My first question - What is the true name of this land? Its ancient name that it has been called since the time of Nerevar.

Good. I am glad you are willing. You show courtesy and that is an excellent sign. The test is simple enough. I will ask three questions about this land and its people. If you answer all three correctly, you will pass. If you answer even one wrong, you will fail.

I see. For some reason, I thought you might be different... That wisdom guided you. I can see I was wrong. I will do you no harm outlander, but I must insist that you leave this place and do not return. We will have no further dealings between us.

Did you see the skulls outside, outlander. They are the skulls of all those who have dared to insult or attack me in my many years in this place. I will not allow you to test my patience, and I will not allow you to distract me further from my holy mission. You will die now!

Greetings outlander. I bear thee no ill will if you bear none against me. I see the look in your eyes... You are curious about this place... about Bal'laku. I might tell you more of this place, and my purpose here, but this is a holy place, and I must know that wisdom guides you before I say anymore. Therefore, I propose a simple test of wisdom. Prove to me that you know something of this land, and I will grant you my hospitality.

Many years ago, I traveled with the previous Incarnate - Peakstar. I suppose I know now that she was a False Incarnate. Somehow, I just always hoped that she might return to me... That if she were truly the Nerevarine... She might... Listen friend. In your travels on the path of the Nerevarine... Have you come across any trace of Peakstar? Do you have any idea of what might have happened to her?

That ring! Let me see that ring outlander! This is 'One-Clan-Under-Moon-and-Star.' Then... You are surely the Nerevarine... I... I am sorry if I doubted you before, friend. I could always tell there was something special about you... That Azura walked with you... It's just... It's time I admit something to you, %PCName.

I have heard whispers on the winds that an outlander had come to the Urshilaku Camp claiming to fulfill the Nerevarine Prophecies. I know you to be that outlander. I truly wish no harm to come to you, so I tell you this now. You are just another in a long line of false incarnates. There is no way that you can fulfill the prophecies, because the Nerevarine has already come before you. I will say no more on this matter, but If you pursue the prophecies any further, it will surely only lead to your death.
You have achieved your destiny, Nerevarine. You are truly the savior of Resdayn.
You are the Nerevarine beyond any doubt. Many have fallen, but you remain. Where all others have failed, you must succeed. If you fail, all is lost.

These towers together are Azura's monument to the Nerevarine, outlander. One tower is symbolic of the curse upon the Tribunal - Nerevar's betrayers. The other is a symbol of Nerevar's inevitable return. The Nerevarine is Azura's promise to the Dunmer that she has not abandoned us, and these towers were her first sign that her prophecy will be fulfilled.
I was right that it would fade away, but I did not forsee it would be your actions that would lead to its deactivation.

It is a curse disguised as a blessing. Just like everything else created by the Tribunal. It does protect Vvardenfell from the beasts of Red Mountain, but at what cost? The bones of nearly every House Dunmer who perishes are now dumped into it in a vain hope to increase its strength by a pitiful amount. It is fueled by the profane magicks of the Tribunal, and it is clear that power is fading. Every year the Ghostfence grows dimmer, and it is only a matter of time before it fades away entirely.

I was once a Gulakhan of the Urshilaku tribe. I may have very well been the one to succeed Sul-Matuul as Ashkhan had I remained with them, but I simply could not. A group of us had a... disagreement with the Ashkhan and Wise Woman some thirty years ago so we set off on our own. We chose Bal'laku as our new home for its significance to our tribe. Over the years the others all lost their way for one reason or another. Now, only I remain here, finding what solace I can in guarding this holy site.
Dagoth Ur has been slain by your hand Nerevar. What this will bring to Resdayn... Only time will tell. You have done your duty as Nerevarine, and I thank you for it.

Dagoth Ur is known as the Sharmat - the Devil of Red Mountain. In his previous life he was a companion of Nerevar and the Tribunal. Whatever he is now... He is simply monstrous... He has brought a curse upon this land far worse than any it has seen before.
The Urshilaku are the last true Velothi in Resdayn. They are the last who still both properly honor the true gods and the ancestors, and the last who remember Azura's promises.
I must insist that you use this land's proper name: Resdayn - I'm afraid that I can tolerate no less outlander.

She is one of the false Tribunal and one of Nerevar's murderers. In her mortal life she was the wife of Nerevar. It seems that their marriage was one of political convenience, so I cannot imagine that Nerevar truly cared for her but I can't know for sure. If he did, then that makes her betrayal all the more loathsome.

Now you know the truth of what happened, and now you will return to Odibael and tell him these truths, and you will tell him... That I am truly sorry... For all the pain and strife that I have caused him. He will have something for you - a staff that I enchanted many years ago. He intends to give it to you all ready. I can feel it even as I watch him now. Tell him these words, and he shall know the truth of your claims. But before you go Nerevarine, I have one more gift to grant you.

I made my way from Bal'laku to Lost Kogoruhn. Even in those days, the Sixth House had already expanded beyond the Ghostfence, and had revived Kogoruhn as its Clanstead. As I walked those terrible halls, I felt that Azura walked with me. If I was truly the Nerevarine, then I knew I would not perish, I could not perish. It was in the deepest and darkest of Kogoruhn's tunnels, that I met the Sharmat's Kin - his general Dagoth Uthol. It was to him that I fell in battle.

We had spent months training and meditating at Bal'laku, and yet the guidance of Azura that I had felt so clearly when living amongst the Urshilaku, only faded with each passing day. I felt that the only way to prove myself as the Nerevarine was to take on the Sixth House directly, and this was something I could not ask Odibael to aid me with. Had I done so, it would have only led to his death.

So Moon-and-Star... You have met my companion of old - Odibael Zebanund. When I followed the Path of the Incarnate, he was my closest ally and my dearest friend. None believed more fervently than he, that I was Nerevar Reborn. It was that dedication that lead him to the life of incredible loneliness that he leads now. His only solace has been his continued sense of duty to both me and to Bal'laku. It has pained me watching him from afar for all these years.
Thank you for all you have done for me. You are a true friend.

%PCName, I hear the truth of your words, and I hear the truth of Peakstar through you. I can feel her blessing upon you. I thank you for this, friend. That after all these years, I finally have some closure. What she spoke to you was true. I have a meager few of Peakstar's former possessions, but this staff is the most cherished one. I give it now to you. You have one duty now, Nerevarine. Where Peakstar failed, you must not. You must follow that Path of the Incarnate to its very end.
You now know about my connection with Peakstar. I would rather not speak anymore of it at this time.

That belt, I would recognize it anywhere. Unassuming, but decently powerful, just like nearly all of her possessions. So you met her spirit in the Cavern of the Incarnate? Did she say what... No... I don't want to know. It's enough to know that she has passed on. But, if her spirit is still in the Cavern... I don't wish to disturb her rest, but would you travel there and ask her one question for me. Will you ask her why she went off on her own, without us? Why did she abandon this place?

Those travel-stained pants, I would recognize them anywhere. Unassuming, but decently powerful, just like nearly all of her possessions. So you met her spirit in the Cavern of the Incarnate? Did she say what... No... I don't want to know. It's enough to know that she has passed on. But, if her spirit is still in the Cavern... I don't wish to disturb her rest, but would you travel there and ask her one question for me. Will you ask her why she went off on her own, without us? Why did she abandon this place?
Please, have you found any evidence of what happened to her? Any trinket or possession of hers you might have come across?
How do you know that name, outlander? Well... It doesn't matter. She is little more than a fairy tale at this point, hardly worth concerning yourself with.
The Ahemmusa are the most traditionalist ashlander tribe aside from the Urshilaku, but even they have fallen far from our true ways.
I would hardly call this life a trade, outlander, but I make my way in this world in my own way, each day after the next.

Bal'laku laid abandoned for many years save for the occasional pilgrimage from members of our tribe. Such pilgrimages ended during my childhood, as they became too dangerous to undertake with any regularity. So now I have returned here as Bal'laku's sole inhabitant. I am glad to be doing what little I can to preserve this site and its history.

And indeed, these towers hold great significance to the Urshilaku... Or at least they did. For hundreds of years in eras past we made our camp here at the base of these towers. They served as our fortress. They inspired us onward through our struggles. But, as the ash upon the land grew ever higher, and the blight from Red Mountain grew thicker, our ancestors moved the camp to the relative safety of the western Ashlands and the shores of the Sea of Ghosts.

As you yourself know, these towers were raised out of the ash by the will of Azura at the exact moment of Nerevar's death. Whether they were always buried under the ash, or manifested by the Prince of Twilight's power, I can't say. Some say they are connected to similar structures nearby in the Ashlands. I cannot say whether this is true either. What I can say is that these towers are a monument to Azura's prophecy of Nerevar's return.
Indoril Nerevar is the ancient hero of the Dunmer people, and the father of our nation of Resdayn. He is revered by all of the Dunmer, including myself.
The Zainab only care for money and trading. In recent days they have become as materialistic as the House Dunmer, and have truly lost their way.
